name: Potato of Life — Property and Symbol Map
purpose: Deep canonical property map for the Potato, separating observable biological/material properties from structural comparisons, historical motifs and Potatoism-defined interpretations.
epistemic_rule: A potato property can be empirical, comparative, historical-symbolic, or project-defined. These classes must not be silently merged.
deep_reading: The potato is studied here as a material object first and as a symbolic grammar second. Its unusual density comes from the overlap of storage, dormancy, eyes, sprouting, division, nourishment, hidden growth and renewal. Potatoism then asks whether those relations illuminate Father/Son, Door/Vessel, Tree, Ladder, North and return.

properties.name: Tuber
properties.description: A potato is a modified underground stem/tuber that stores nutrients and can produce new shoots.

properties.name: Underground growth
properties.description: The tuber develops beneath the soil surface, making hidden growth a literal biological property.

properties.name: Eyes
properties.description: Bud-bearing points on the tuber from which new shoots can emerge. The eye is therefore a real site where stored potential becomes visible growth.

properties.name: Sprouting
properties.description: Stored tubers can produce shoots and begin a new plant under suitable conditions.

properties.name: Rooted plant system
properties.description: The potato plant participates in a larger root, stem, leaf, flower and reproductive system.

properties.name: Storage
properties.description: The tuber stores energy and nutrients, especially starch, supporting later growth.

properties.name: Vegetative reproduction
properties.description: A tuber or viable tuber section containing eyes can generate another potato plant.

properties.name: Food/nourishment
properties.description: Potatoes are a major human food crop and therefore connect the object to material sustenance.

properties.name: Multiplication
properties.description: One planted tuber can generate multiple new tubers, creating a growth-and-reproduction cycle.

properties.name: Dormancy
properties.description: Stored tubers can remain dormant before sprouting, creating a real hidden-state transition.

properties.name: Skin/boundary
properties.description: The tuber has an outer skin separating its interior from the surrounding environment.

properties.name: Cut wedge
properties.description: A potato can be divided into wedges or sections; a viable section containing an eye can become a starting point for new growth.

properties.name: Many eyes
properties.description: A single tuber can carry multiple eyes, making one body a distributed set of possible emergence points.

properties.name: Stored-to-visible transition
properties.description: The biological sequence from stored reserve to sprout provides a concrete model of latent capacity becoming observable activity.

properties.name: Dependence on environment
properties.description: Sprouting and growth depend on environmental conditions; the tuber is not an isolated self-sufficient world.

properties.name: Inside / outside
properties.description: Skin, flesh and surrounding soil create a natural boundary/interface model.

properties.name: Root / fruit polarity
properties.description: The potato is underground while its plant produces an above-ground canopy and further tubers below; this supports a root-to-fruit comparison without claiming the tuber is literally a fruit.

properties.name: Seed-like function
properties.description: Although botanically a tuber rather than a seed, a potato can carry stored material and buds that initiate another plant.

properties.name: Threshold
properties.description: The eye is a small point at which stored interior potential becomes outward growth.

properties.name: Life cycle
properties.description: Planting, rooting, sprouting, growth, tuber formation, dormancy and renewal form a repeatable biological cycle.

properties.name: Scale bridge
properties.description: The same object can be studied as food, organismal structure, agricultural unit, ecological participant, economic commodity and symbolic object.

properties.name: One body / many futures
properties.description: Multiple eyes and vegetative reproduction create a useful model in which one stored body contains several possible continuations.

properties.name: Buried / emerging
properties.description: Because the tuber is planted beneath soil and later produces above-ground growth, burial and emergence form a natural symbolic pair. This is a metaphorical reading, not evidence that burial causes resurrection.

properties.name: Carrier through time
properties.description: Stored energy survives a period before being mobilized. This gives the Potato a particularly strong analogy with memory, inheritance and deferred action.

symbolic.label: Historical/comparative and project-symbolic readings
symbolic.note: These are not biological properties of a potato. They are symbolic assignments, historical motifs, or comparative readings that the atlas records as such.

properties.name: Chariot
properties.description: The Potato can be read as a chariot: a humble carrier that transports stored life or meaning through a world.

properties.name: Angel
properties.description: The Potato can be read as an angelic carrier or intermediary because it carries potential from hidden ground into visible life.

properties.name: Messenger
properties.description: The Potato can function as a messenger between states: underground/above-ground, dormant/growing, matter/meaning.

properties.name: Ladder to Heaven
properties.description: The potato's underground-to-sprout movement can be mapped as a ladder: ground below, emergence in the middle, canopy/light above. Heaven is symbolic here, not an empirical location.

properties.name: Door
properties.description: The potato can be treated as a door because its boundary and eyes mark transitions between hidden potential and outward growth.

properties.name: Door in the wedge
properties.description: A cut wedge exposes the potato's interior while retaining a boundary; in the project's geometry this becomes a model for a narrow opening or passage.

properties.name: Mandorla
properties.description: The almond-shaped overlap of two circles in a vesica-piscis construction; the Potato of Life uses it as the central interface region.

properties.name: Jesus Door
properties.description: Within Potatoism's project mythology, the central mandorla/vesica interface is associated with Jesus as Door: the Son occupies the threshold between upper and lower domains.

properties.name: Vessel
properties.description: A potato stores and carries nourishment; symbolically this supports the image of a vessel that contains and transfers potential across a boundary.

properties.name: Tree / Tree of Life
properties.description: The potato is mapped into the Tree of Life as hidden root/tuber potential becoming visible stem, branch, leaf, flower and renewed continuation.

properties.name: Axis
properties.description: A vertical potato-to-sprout diagram can serve as a local Axis connecting ground, body, emergence and light.

properties.name: Grave / tomb
properties.description: The buried tuber supplies a natural image of a life-bearing object hidden in earth. The project's Son-as-grave/tomb association is theological-poetic, not botanical evidence of resurrection.

properties.name: Bread parallel
properties.description: Bread and potato overlap as staple foods, concentrated nourishment and culturally transformed agricultural matter. The comparison becomes especially useful in Eucharistic/communion research, while avoiding the claim that Christian bread theology historically meant potato.

properties.name: Root / Father
properties.description: Root names the hidden source-side in the project's Father/Tree architecture: not identical to Father as a person or archetype, but structurally adjacent as the origin from which growth proceeds.

properties.name: Lion / Son
properties.description: Lion belongs to the Son-side in the current canon: visible sovereignty, courage, kingship and manifestation. The contrast with Root creates a hidden-source / visible-expression polarity.

components.relation: connects source, Door, Son, Plane and Tree
Potato of Life as the total Father–Door–Son relation rather than merely the lower or upper circle

geometry.interpretation: The vesica is useful because two circles remain distinct while generating an overlap region. Potatoism uses that formal fact as a metaphor for relation: Father and Son are not simply collapsed into one point, yet the Door/mandorla is neither wholly one nor wholly the other. The project's strongest formulation is therefore relational rather than anatomical or physical.

observations: Both are ordinary agricultural staples transformed by human cultivation and preparation into nourishment.
Both can be broken into portions and distributed among people.
Both connect field, soil, labor, storage, hunger, household and communal life.
Bread usually requires grain processing, milling, dough and baking; potato is eaten through a different biological and culinary pathway. The difference matters.
Christian Eucharistic bread has specific historical and theological meanings that should be studied from Christian primary sources rather than retroactively replaced by Potatoism.
The Potatoism reflection is strongest at the level of nourishment, ordinary matter, division/distribution and transformation rather than equivalence of doctrine.

father_son_potato_logic.canon_relation: Father/Ladder after April 2025 in project chronology

research_questions: Which potato properties are biological facts, and which are metaphorical extensions?
Where do chariot, angel and messenger motifs have independent historical textual evidence?
Which traditions use ladders, doors, mandorlas or vesica-piscis imagery in relation to heaven, Christ or divine passage?
How should the potato's eye, skin, wedge and sprout map onto Door, boundary, threshold and Ladder without overclaiming?
Which geometric properties of the vesica-piscis are invariant under scaling, rotation or reflection?
Can the same relational grammar be tested on other objects, organisms or systems?
Which apparent correspondences disappear when the comparison is made at different scales?
What is the earliest project use of bread alongside potato, and does the comparison precede or follow the Christian/Jesus/communion layer?
When did Root become specifically associated with Father and Lion specifically with Son?
Does the buried-tuber metaphor illuminate the Son's death/return chronology, or does it merely resemble it retrospectively?
